title: Number of Distinct Islands
summary: Given an m x n binary matrix, count the number of distinct islands.
statement: Given an m x n binary matrix, count the number of distinct islands. Islands are groups of 1's connected horizontally or vertically. Two islands are the same if one can be moved to match the other without rotation or reflection.
constraints: Grid cells are zero or one; islands connect orthogonally.
Two islands are equal only by translation, not rotation or reflection.
hints: Translation invariance is achieved by coordinates relative to each island’s origin.
Flood-fill each unseen island and store its sorted relative cell offsets.
Subtract the start row/column from every visited cell; add the tuple to a set.
Translated copies produce identical offset sets, while any different orthogonal shape differs at some relative cell.
editorial: Translated copies produce identical offset sets, while any different orthogonal shape differs at some relative cell.

tests.explanation: The two translated 2x2 islands have one distinct shape.
The bent island and isolated cell produce two shapes.
